title: Bryson DeChambeau was ‘make or break’ in LIV Golf collapse
article_text:

Not many bought into the LIV product more than DeChambeau. One of the marquee names to quit the PGA Tour in return for Saudi millions, the breakaway circuit saw the two-time US Open champion come into his own on and off the golf course.

While a reduced schedule seemingly allowed him to tap into his passion for YouTube golf away from the action, when it came to teeing it up competitively, not many performed better on the LIV setup.

In five seasons in Crushers GC colours, DeChambeau won five LIV events, banked almost $70 million in prize money, and also secured a second major triumph at the 2024 US Open.

Last week, LIV’s demise was finally confirmed in a bankruptcy court in New Jersey, after proposed investor, BC Partners Credit, opted not to press forward with a transaction that would have made LIV’s 2.0 plans a reality.

The beginning of the end came seven months earlier, after the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia (PIF) opted to cut ties with the breakaway league.

It is understood that the LIV product could have ceased to exist there and then, however, league officials – led by CEO, Scott O’Neil – mustered up a plan in a matter of days to keep things afloat in 2026, before looking to move into 2027 and beyond.

These plans are what we now know as ‘LIV 2.0’. The project was LIV Golf stripped back, but while the Saudi riches were no more, it did give the league a chance to survive nonetheless.

These survival hopes, however, laid on the commitment of its players. As the 2026 season came to a premature end in August, a number of the LIV membership were already beginning to explore options elsewhere.

DeChambeau meanwhile was seemingly standing strong with O’Neil and co. So much so, the Crushers skipper led an all-player meeting at LIV’s penultimate event in New York at the end of the summer, in the hopes of rallying up support behind the new investor and 2.0.

The coming months, though, would prove difficult. After LIV’s campaign ended with the cancellation of the Team Championship, the battle for survival was well and truly on.

When bankruptcy protection was filed in October, it soon became apparent that LIV needed a ‘critical mass’ of players in order to make 2.0 work. With Jon Rahm heading for the exit door, the most important name in all of this was that of DeChambeau’s.

As players slowly started to leave, and LIV’s deadline for player commitments continued to be extended, DeChambeau remained quiet. At this time, bunkered.co.uk understands that he was in close contact with both the investor and league chiefs in regard to how things could move forward.

Eventually, though, something had to give, and while the 33-year-old had seemingly been keen to see the product press on, he later made the decision not to sign up to the league’s new terms.

“Bryson was always going to be the make or break player,” a LIV source told bunkered.co.uk. Those involved were under the influence that DeChambeau was all in on the 2.0 plans in the weeks leading up to last week’s decision, before making the late call to step away.

“That felt like the final nail in the coffin,” the source added.

Three days after LIV’s winding down and liquidation process was announced, DeChambeau broke his silence. “I’m not going to rewrite the last four years,” he said in a statement on social media.

He went on to thank those involved, before adding: “I still believe in team golf. It may look different in the future, but I still believe it’s essential to growing the game.”

Just how that may work remains to be seen. In his social media appearances in recent weeks, DeChambeau has dropped his Crushers GC apparel, appearing to signal the end of his LIV-based brand.

From an individual point of view, the American will return to action in South Africa next month via a tournament invite in the Gary Player-hosted Nedbank Golf Challenge.

With the PGA Tour door seemingly closed until next August, the DP World Tour could well become DeChambeau’s new home until then. If this is the case, he has until the end of this week to apply for membership, having earned exemption through his US Open win two years ago.

title: Bryson DeChambeau admits ‘I’ve said things that didn’t help’ after LIV collapse
article_text:
BRYSON DECHAMBEAU has admitted he “said some things that didn’t help” during the feud between LIV Golf and the PGA Tour.

The American, 33, published a lengthy social media statement on Sunday as controversial breakaway tour LIV prepares to enter liquidation.

Signing DeChambeau in 2022 was one of LIV’s early coups, and he was quickly caught up in the legal storm between the Saudi-backed tour and the PGA Tour, arguing that the PGA had an illegal monopoly over competitive golf.

But LIV is now winding down after Saudi Arabia pulled their funding and viable new backing for a ‘2.0’ version of the tour never materialised.

DeChambeau wrote on X: “I am not going to rewrite the last four years.

“I made a decision I believed in, and I’m grateful for what came with it: playing in front of fans new and old around the world who rarely got to see the best players at home.

“The record crowds in Adelaide and Johannesburg will stick with me for the rest of my life.

“I believed this game could reach more people, in more places, in a new way. I still believe that. And I gave it everything I had to keep team golf alive.

“I still believe in team golf. It may look different in the future, but I still believe it’s essential to growing the game.

“Arnold Palmer said no player is bigger than the game, and I want to acknowledge that, along the way, I’ve said some things that didn’t help.”

DeChambeau revealed he will play at the Nedbank Golf Challenge next month, which will be his first DP World Tour start in almost six years.

The two-time US Open champion qualifies for DP World Tour playing privileges if he wishes to return to regular competition.

He could alternatively rely on invitations and exemptions into tournaments, or focus on his YouTube channel, which has over 3million subscribers.

DeChambeau must wait 12 months from the date of his final LIV appearance before he is eligible to make a PGA Tour return, which would be highly controversial given the events of the past four years.

He added: “Whatever comes next, I’ll approach it with humility and respect for the people who carried this game long before me.

“I’ll go about whatever is next the right way. My passion has been to grow this game. That’s still the goal.”

title: Lakshya Sen Leads Indian Charge At Kumamoto Masters
article_text:
India's top badminton stars, including Lakshya Sen and the formidable duo Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, are set to battle at the Kumamoto Masters Japan Super 500, aiming to secure crucial points for qualification to the prestigious BWF World Tour Finals.

- Lakshya Sen, currently 10th in BWF World Tour rankings, needs to break into the top eight to qualify for the season-ending tournament in China.

- Sen will open his campaign against world No. 24 Chi Yu Jen of Chinese Taipei at the Kumamoto Masters Japan Super 500 tournament, beginning on Tuesday.

- Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, world No. 6, aim to regain form after recent early exits, facing Wang Chang and Xie Haonan of China.

- Other Indian participants include Kidambi Srikanth, Malvika Bansod, Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, and mixed doubles pairs.

- The BWF World Tour Finals will be held from December 9 to 13, making strong performances this week and next week crucial for qualification.

Bolstered by a timely win at Germany, India ace shuttler Lakshya Sen will look to strengthen his bid for a place in the season-ending BWF World Tour Finals when he competes at the USD 500,000 Kumamoto Masters Japan Super 500 tournament, beginning here on Tuesday.

World No. 13 Lakshya, who ended a difficult phase by returning to the podium at the Hylo Open, will open his campaign against world No. 24 Chi Yu Jen of Chinese Taipei.

The eighth-seeded Indian is currently 10th in the BWF World Tour rankings and needs to break into the top eight to qualify for the season-ending tournament in China. The 25-year-old from Almora has a 1-1 head-to-head record against Chi, and a strong showing this week and at next week's Hong Kong Open Super 500 could be enough to secure his place.

The BWF World Tour Finals will be held from December 9 to 13.

India's Kidambi Srikanth, who reached the US Open final in June this year, is also in the men's singles draw and will face Denmark's Rasmus Gemke.

In women's singles, Malvika Bansod will take on fifth seed Tomoka Miyazaki of Japan.

World No. 6 and sixth seeds Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will look to rediscover their winning touch after three successive first-round exits since their China Masters title. The Indian pair, who failed to defend their gold medal at the Asian Games, will face fifth seeds Wang Chang and Xie Haonan of China.

Satwik and Chirag, who also won the Singapore Open earlier this year, are 12th in the BWF World Tour rankings with 58,550 points. However, BWF rules allow a maximum of two pairs from a country to qualify for the World Tour Finals, provided they finish inside the top eight.

Currently, only Indonesia and Malaysia have two pairs each inside the top eight, with South Korea, England, China and Denmark also represented.

Hariharan Amsakarunan and MR Arjun will face Malaysia's third seeds Aaron Chia and Soh Wooi Yik.

In women's doubles, Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, who won India's maiden bronze medal in the event at the World Championships in August, will take on Japan's Hinata Suzuki and Nao Yamakita.

The scratch mixed doubles pairing of Hariharan and Tanisha Crasto will face top seeds Jiang Zhen Bang and Wei Ya Xin of China, while Dhruv Rawat and K. Maneesha will meet fourth seeds Ye Hong Wei and Nicole Gonzales Chan of Chinese Taipei.

ATP opens two new sponsorship categories for Julius Baer partnership
article_text:
The top-tier ATP men’s tennis tour has announced a wide-ranging global partnership with Swiss wealth management group Julius Baer, as it continues to strengthen its commercial portfolio.

The new agreement gives ATP two new sponsorship categories, with Julius Baer to serve as the tour’s first official wealth management partner and the first official partner of the ATP Coaches Programme, which supports 230 coaches through education, visibility, recognition, and commercial opportunities.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

As part of the agreement, from 2027, Julius Baer will activate at five ATP tournaments, including the Chile Open in Santiago, the Munich Open in Germany, the Mallorca Open in Spain, the Japan Open in Tokyo, and Swiss Indoors Basel.

For the Swiss Indoors Basel, Julius Baer will also serve as the tournament's presenting partner.

Beyond the five events, Julius Baer will gain access to ATP experiences and premium hospitality at a wide range of tournaments throughout the season, with the company offering its guests opportunities with players, tennis clinics, and behind-the-scenes access.

As the official partner of the ATP Coaches Programme, Julius Baer will work with a group of ATP coaches and present the ATP Coach Spotlight series and Coach of the Year recognition across the tour’s social channels.

The wealth management group will also gain branding on the ‘coaches’ corner’ at select tournaments, as well as a co-branded official ATP coaches cap worn in the coaches’ box.

The new global partnership comes as the ATP continues to strengthen its commercial partnership slate, having re-elected Andrea Gaudenzi as chairman of the ATP for a third term in January until 2028.

Most recently, the ATP announced a new multi-year partnership with US tennis brand K-Swiss, which will serve as the tour’s new official footwear partner.

Under the partnership, K-Swiss will provide footwear to ATP umpires, physios, and key officials, as well as players who do not have an existing footwear sponsor.

Earlier this year, the tour secured a new multi-year agreement with global investment organization EQT to serve as the tour’s first official private markets partner through 2030, while extending its long-standing digital partnership with Indian digital services and consulting company Infosys.

The organization also renewed its partnership with video streaming technology firm Deltatre, covering graphics, data, and production across the 2026 season, and expanded its behind-the-scenes content partnership with Overtime, the youth-focused US sports media company, to boost its younger fanbase.

The ATP also announced global content partnerships with TikTok and Spotify, as well as launching global marketing campaigns and a new brand identity.

title: Strauss strengthens growing UEFA ties with Euro 2028 sponsorship
article_text:
Workwear brand Engelbert Strauss has expanded its relationship with European soccer’s governing body UEFA by becoming the latest sponsor of Euro 2028.

The German company will serve as a global sponsor of UEFA’s flagship men’s national team competition, strengthening its long-standing partnership with the body.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The agreement builds on Strauss’ involvement as the official workwear partner of UEFA Euro 2024 in Germany. The brand has also been a partner of the UEFA Europa League and UEFA Conference League club competitions since 2021.

Strauss was also recently named as the first-ever official partner of the UEFA Refereeing division, in an agreement running through 2028-29.

As part of that three-year agreement, the Strauss logo features on the sleeves of UEFA referees' kits, with the deal extending across all major UEFA national team and club competitions. Branding will also be visible on VAR monitors and within UEFA's Video Operations Room.

As a global sponsor of Euro 2028, the brand will receive exclusive marketing and promotional rights, including brand visibility throughout the tournament and fan engagement opportunities across the host nations and other global markets.

Strauss will further extend its presence and engagement throughout the tournament by supporting the Referee Assistant's Escort S&E programme.

The company is seeking to use the Euro 2028 partnership to develop its presence in the United Kingdom, one of its key international growth markets.

Henning Strauss, CEO and owner of Strauss, said: “UEFA Euro 2028 offers us a unique platform to further expand our presence in the British market and reach new audiences – from professional users to retail partners.”

Last month, Betano, the sports betting brand owned by Kaizen Gaming, also extended its partnership with UEFA to become a Euro 2028 sponsor, while Chinese electronics brand Hisense renewed its long-running tie-up with the continental body in September to cover the tournament.

Other Euro 2028 partners announced in recent months include online travel booking platform Booking.com and BT Group, the heavyweight UK telecoms firm.

The tournament will take place across eight host cities and nine stadiums in England, Wales, Scotland, and Ireland from June 9 to July 9, 2028.

The CAA Eleven agency markets commercial rights to UEFA’s national teams competitions under the current cycle but will be replaced by sports media and commercial agency Relevent after Euro 2028.

Relevent was recently awarded an eight-year contract running through 2036, covering future editions of the men's Euros in 2032 and 2036, as well as the 2029 and 2033 women's editions.

The agreement covers sponsorship sales, media rights, licensing, and other associated commercial rights.

CAA Eleven was set up in 2012 to manage the UEFA partnership.

title: ATP Rankings: Alcaraz closes the gap, Djokovic drops, Fritz +2, Ruud +5, van Assche +13, Hijikata +24

Carlos Alcaraz has closed the gap to the top two in the ATP Rankings following his Paris Masters triumph, while Novak Djokovic and Taylor Fritz are among the players on the move.

World No 3 Alcaraz defeated fourth-ranked Ben Shelton 7-6(5), 7-5 in the championship match in Paris to claim his maiden title at the indoor hard-court Masters 1000 event.

The Spaniard’s victory has increased his points total by 1,000 to 7,100, which has moved him to within 2,350 points of second-placed Jannik Sinner and 2,450 points of world No 1 Alexander Zverev.

Sinner has not played since Wimbledon due to a knee injury, while Zverev lost to Lorenzo Musetti in his opening match in Paris — which was his first match after becoming world No 1.

Fritz’s run to the quarter-finals in the French capital has lifted him two places to world No 10, with Rafael Jodar and Djokovic dropping to 11th and 12th respectively.

Casper Ruud has soared from 23rd to 18th after reaching the semi-finals in Paris, while Learner Tien has fallen from 19th to 22nd.

title: Yamaguchi Targets Kumamoto Title as An Withdraws
article_text:
[Sports Chosun Kim Ga-eul] Yamaguchi Akane (World No. 2, Japan) eyes the top spot in the absence of 'world’s strongest' An Se-young (Samsung Life Insurance).

The 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Kumamoto Masters (Super 500) will take place in Kumamoto, Japan, from the 10th to the 15th. The women’s singles event features Yamaguchi, Wang Zhiyi, Chen Yufei (both from China), Ratchanok Intanon (Thailand), and others. However, An Se-young will not participate. After a recent hectic schedule, An Se-young has decided to skip the Kumamoto Masters to rest and regroup. She aims to target a historic 12th win at the BWF World Tour Finals (December 9–13, Hangzhou, China). An Se-young said, "I’m not focusing too much on the record. I’ll try to play my own game in the next tournament."

With An Se-young temporarily absent, competition for the throne is expected to intensify. Particularly, attention is focused on Yamaguchi, who is competing on home soil.

Japan’s 'J Sports' reported on the 9th, "Can Yamaguchi win at home? The results of this tournament and the subsequent Hong Kong Open will determine the participants for the BWF World Tour Finals. This is the final sprint for qualification. Although Yamaguchi has already secured a spot in the Finals, attention is on whether she can claim her second victory in her hometown. Can she achieve her second win in Kumamoto after two years? She has recently competed in major tournaments and is currently in the process of regaining her form. The key is how much she can elevate her condition. Yamaguchi has been assigned the first seed after An Se-young withdrew." Yamaguchi is the 2024 champion of this tournament.

Yamaguchi won the silver medal at the Korea Open (Super 500), which concluded on the 8th. She lost to An Se-young in the final with a game score of 1-2 (12-21, 21-15, 16-21). Yamaguchi has lost 11 consecutive matches against An Se-young. After the match, An Se-young said, "Yamaguchi is a player who brings new plays to every match, making it difficult to adapt. However, there are habitual plays that emerge. I calmly wait and aim to score confidently. When you keep giving points, you might get impatient, but thinking ‘it’s okay’ even after mistakes, confidently making them, and acknowledging the opponent’s good plays helps in navigating the match."

Kim Ga-eul, Staff Reporter epi17@sportschosun.com

title: ATP signs global partnership with Julius Baer
article_text:
The ATP has signed a multi-year partnership with Swiss wealth management group Julius Baer, which becomes the ATP’s first Official Wealth Management Partner and the first Official Partner of the ATP Coaches Programme.

Currently supporting over 230 coaches, the ATP Coaches Programme enhances the Tour experience of ATP coaches through education, visibility, recognition, and commercial opportunities. The programme recognises the important role coaches play in the long-term development of players and their impact on the game globally.

Julius Baer’s role as the first Official Partner of the ATP Coaches Programme marks an important step in bringing new benefits to the ATP ecosystem. Julius Baer will work with a group of ATP coaches and will have branding on the Coaches Corner at select tournaments, as well as a co-branded Official ATP Coaches Cap worn in the coaches’ box and available through ATP’s official retail channels.

Across the ATP’s social channels, Julius Baer will present the ATP Coach Spotlight series and the Coach of the Year recognition.

From 2027, Julius Baer will activate at five ATP tournaments across Europe, Asia and South America: the BCI Seguros Chile Open in Santiago, BMW Open in Munich, Vanda Pharmaceuticals Mallorca Championships, Kinoshita Group Japan Open Tennis Championships in Tokyo and Swiss Indoors Basel. Julius Baer will become Presenting Partner in Basel, pairing a leading Swiss brand with Switzerland’s premier ATP event.

Beyond these events, Julius Baer will have access to ATP experiences and premium hospitality at a wide range of tournaments throughout the season. Delivering world-class, innovative experiences for Julius Baer’s key guests is central to the partnership and will include player activation, tennis clinics and behind-the-scenes access.

Eno Polo, ATP CEO, said: “Julius Baer is our first Official Wealth Management Partner, which marks a major milestone for the Tour. We’re delighted that they have chosen to invest in tennis and share our commitment to creating new benefits across the ATP ecosystem. The launch of the ATP Coaches Programme is a clear example of how we can strengthen the game together and we look forward to seeing what more we can achieve through our partnership.”

Stefan Bollinger, Julius Baer CEO, said: “With over 130 years of Swiss heritage, we are especially proud to demonstrate our long-term commitment to our home market by becoming Presenting Partner of the Swiss Indoors Basel, one of Switzerland’s most iconic sporting events and a premier tournament on the professional tennis calendar. Together with our ATP Tour partnership from 2027, this collaboration reflects our broader engagement in tennis and our ambition to create meaningful experiences for clients and fans alike. One of the most inspiring aspects of tennis is the relationship between athlete and coach: Success rarely happens alone. It is built through trust, guidance and long-term commitment. Those same qualities underpin how we work with our clients. We look forward to being part of the tournament’s journey and helping shape its success in the years ahead.”

The partnership will provide global exposure, VIP experiences and other benefits at each tournament, building brand recognition across major markets.

The announcement builds on a period of record growth in new partnerships for the ATP, underlining the strength of the Tour as a premium platform for brand visibility, business engagement and international expansion.

title: Ahn Se-young aims to set badminton record with 12 wins in a season
article_text:
Ahn Se-young (24, Samsung Life Insurance) is chasing an unprecedented 12 tournament wins in a single season in badminton history. Having already recorded 11 wins in a season for the second straight year, she has a chance to make new history at the final tournament of the year.

World No. 1 Ahn Se-young beat world No. 2 Akane Yamaguchi of Japan 2-1 (21-12, 15-21, 21-16) in the women's singles final of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Korea Open (Super 500) held on the 8th at Jinnam Gymnasium in Yeosu, South Jeolla.

Ahn Se-young reclaimed the Korea Open title for the first time since 2023 and captured her third tournament win at this event. She also avenged the loss she suffered to Yamaguchi in last year's final.

With this victory, Ahn Se-young notched her 11th win of the season. She matched the single-season record for most singles wins set last year by herself and by Kento Momota of Japan in 2019. Notably, she became the first player in badminton history to record 11 wins in a season in two consecutive years.

Her next target is an unprecedented 12 wins in a season.

Taiwanese outlet Liberty Times noted, "The invincible queen Ahn Se-young may produce two astonishing records this year," and highlighted the possibility she could set a new record at the year-end BWF World Tour Finals.

Ahn Se-young has a 71-1 record in 72 matches this season. Her winning percentage is an astonishing 98.6%. Since losing to Wang Zhiyi of China in the All England Open final in March, she has compiled a 55-match winning streak.

Her winning streak, too, is on the brink of setting a new record.

Indonesian legend Susi Susanti recorded a 59-match winning streak in women's singles from 1993 to 1994. If Ahn Se-young wins four more matches, she will tie that record; five more wins would put her at 60 consecutive victories.

If Ahn Se-young wins all five matches at the World Tour Finals to take the title, she would achieve both 12 wins in a season and a 60-match winning streak in women's singles at the same time.

Ahn Se-young plans to rest and regroup for the time being. The heavy schedule this year has left fatigue in her ankles and knees. She is reportedly not entering the Kumamoto Masters in Japan or the Hong Kong Open.

Her next target is the BWF World Tour Finals, which will be held in Hangzhou, China, from Dec. 9 to 13.

After winning the Korea Open, Ahn Se-young smiled and said of being called the greatest of all time (GOAT), "I'm grateful just to hear that. I still have many days left to play. When my career is over, I'll think about whether I'm the GOAT or not."

Having already recorded 11 wins in a season for two straight years, Ahn Se-young is now aiming for territory no one has reached. If she tops the year-end Finals, she will write a new chapter in history with 12 tournament wins in a single season.

title: PTO brings Saxo Bank in as Dubai event partner

title: Bombay Sapphire takes title rights to E1’s season finale
article_text:
The event will be E1’s first double-header and its second visit to Miami, with teams backed by owners including Tom Brady, LeBron James, Steve Aoki and Marc Anthony. As title partner, the English gin brand’s name sits alongside the event title and logo, and appears on co-branded event and digital materials at the race venue and around the city.

The partnership has grown through the season. Bombay Sapphire activated at E1 races in Lake Como and Ibiza, and is presenting partner of the E1 Blue Impact Championship, which encourages teams to support aquatic conservation and restoration. That focus on water ties in with the brand’s own sustainability story: its 10 botanicals come from certified sustainable suppliers and are vapour-infused at Laverstoke Mill in Hampshire, where the gin is made.

In Miami, the brand will run activations in the build-up to the race weekend and across both race days. Its Bombay Sapphire Sparkling Lemon, E1’s cocktail, will be served at venues across the city.

Sanctioned by the Union Internationale Motonautique, E1 races electric RaceBirds in waterfront cities including Jeddah, Lake Como, Monaco and Lagos, with each team fielding one male and one female pilot.

Jamie Copas, Chief Executive Officer at E1, said, “We’re delighted that our long-term partnership with Bombay Sapphire continues to grow and for them to now become title partner for the Bombay Sapphire E1 Miami GP 2026 race double-header.“

“We look forward to working with Bombay Sapphire to bring the partnership to life in Miami as we gear up for a landmark event, with the Championship’s first-ever double-header set to bring the 2026 season to a thrilling close.”

Tara King, Senior Director, North America at Bombay Sapphire, said, “Bombay Sapphire’s ‘Step Into The Blue’ is our invitation to immerse in the beauty of life, and E1 is the ultimate expression of that. This is a fresh addition to the global sports category, bringing all-electric raceboat competition to waterfront cities around the world and drawing attention to the waters that make the sport possible.“

“As Title Partner in Miami, we’re bringing that same spirit of discovery beyond the water and into the city – with the Bombay Sapphire Sparkling Lemon as the championship’s official cocktail, we’re giving new audiences an approachable way to discover gin and join the race weekend celebrations across Miami.”

title: Lady Cranes win Rugby Africa Women’s 7s to qualify for HSBC Division III
article_text:
Uganda’s Lady Cranes 7s defeated Tunisia Ladies 33-00 to lift the prestigious Rugby Africa Women’s 7s in Nairobi, Kenya.

The Lady Cranes went unbeaten across the two days, only conceding a combined 31 points against South Africa ‘A’ and Kenya Lionesses on Day 2, while scoring 216 in 6 games.

In the final, Tunisia started off strong, putting Uganda on the back foot, but the Lady Cranes stayed patient, as they have been, turning over possession after forcing a handling error.

Uganda then opened the scoring through Lydia Namabiro, who carried hard and gained post-contact meters to go across the try line. Tina Akello’s conversion gave Uganda a 7-point lead to calm the waters at the RFUEA Grounds.

Uganda’s discipline then went wanting as they conceded back-to-back penalties. Replacement scrumhalf Mastula Namboozo was unfortunately found on the wrong end of the law as her tackle on the dipping Tunisian was adjudged to be high, sending her to the sin bin for 2 minutes.

Despite being 6 players on the pitch, the Cranes stayed focused and got another try through Namabiro, with Akello converting. Another try-scoring opportunity opened up for Uganda, but Peace Lekuru’s attempt over the ruck was rather cynical, with the try disallowed and a penalty awarded to Tunisia.

In the second half, Suzan Adong scored for Uganda after a beautiful switch pass from Namboozo put her in the gap. Namboozo added the extra 2 points, but Uganda’s indiscipline came back to the fore again as substitute Gertrude Kateesa received a yellow card soon after coming on in the second half.

Namabiro once again got on the scoresheet, completing her hat-trick and putting Uganda in a comfortable position. Unfortunately for Namboozo, her conversion attempt from the left of the uprights hit the crossbar, leaving the score at 26-00 for Uganda.

Uganda’s Lady Cranes were not yet done despite the margin being clear. title: Sid Lee Sport partners with Guinness to measure the true commercial value of sports sponsorship
article_text:
Major evaluation project spans six markets and nine rights holders, moving beyond traditional media valuation to assess the business impact of Guinness’s global sponsorship portfolio.

Global sports marketing agency Sid Lee Sport, working alongside sister agency, Kepler, is undertaking a major evaluation of Guinness’s global sports sponsorship portfolio, designed to establish a clearer understanding of the commercial impact of its football and rugby partnerships.

The project covers six key markets – Great Britain, Ireland, Kenya, the United States, Indonesia and South Korea – and nine rights holders, including the Premier League, Arsenal, Aston Villa, Newcastle United, the Guinness Men’s and Women’s Six Nations and the four home rugby unions.

Sid Lee Sport and Kepler’s combined evaluation uses KIP, a custom-built, proprietary intelligence platform, to analyse three years of sales, brand and partnership data, helping isolate the incremental commercial impact of Guinness’s sponsorship investments.

The analysis goes beyond exposure, examining broadcast media value, digital reach, stadium pouring rights, fan research and experiential activation, alongside how effectively each partnership is utilised across different markets.

The evaluation aims to provide Guinness with a consistent, commercially grounded understanding of sponsorship performance across markets and partners, helping inform future investment decisions and identify opportunities to unlock greater value from its portfolio.

Mike Grumbridge, Managing Director at Sid Lee Sport, said: “The sponsorship industry continues to rely heavily on traditional metrics such as media exposure and reach to demonstrate value, but that doesn’t necessarily tell brands what their investment is delivering commercially.

“Our work with Guinness is about going much further. By combining the proprietary intelligence model of Sid Lee Sport and Kepler with deep sponsorship expertise, we’re building a clearer picture of where sponsorship creates genuine business value and how brands can unlock more of it.

“We believe this represents an important step forward in how sponsorship effectiveness is understood and measured.”

“Guinness is a brand steeped in sporting heritage and renowned for its innovation. Working with Sid Lee Sport has helped us define how we shape our brand in sport,” said Paddy Carberry, Guinness Global Marketing Manager, Head of Sport.

The Guinness project reflects Sid Lee Sport’s wider commitment to helping brands unlock more value from sport, bringing together world-class creativity, deep sponsorship expertise and a focus on effectiveness.

Tomorrow, (November 10) Sid Lee Sport and Guinness will host ‘From Pitch to Pint’, a live Unofficial Partner podcast at its London headquarters, bringing together representatives from the brand and agency to explore the true value of sponsorship.

The discussion will examine how brands can move beyond traditional measurement approaches and develop a more meaningful understanding of the returns generated by their partnerships. To register your interest in attending, sign up here.

title: VAST Ghana rejects GFA push to Relax Alcohol Sponsorship Rules
article_text:
Vision for Accelerated Sustainable Development Ghana (VAST Ghana) has drawn a firm line in Ghana’s debate over alcohol sponsorship in sport. The civil society organisation has rejected the Ghana Football Association’s renewed appeal for the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) to relax restrictions, insisting that public health protections must remain intact.

The dispute began after GFA President Kurt Edwin Simeon-Okraku told Parliament’s Youth and Sports Committee that current FDA restrictions had denied Ghanaian football a major commercial opportunity. He said a proposed partnership with Guinness Ghana, reportedly worth more than US$5 million annually for the Ghana Premier League, collapsed after the FDA declined to approve it.

For the GFA, the argument is straightforward: domestic football needs sustainable funding, stronger clubs, better infrastructure, and greater commercial appeal. Okraku argued that the restrictions deprive the sport of private-sector investment and urged Parliament to review the provision that gives the FDA authority to approve or reject alcohol-company sponsorship agreements.

VAST Ghana sees the issue differently. While acknowledging that football requires reliable financing, the organisation argues that commercial gains cannot justify weakening safeguards designed to protect children from alcohol advertising and normalise drinking among young audiences.

In its statement, VAST Ghana warned that Ghana must not sacrifice public health for the interests of an industry whose products are linked to preventable disease, injury, disability, and premature death. The group’s central message is that sports financing should not become a route through which harmful products gain visibility among children and young people.

The FDA restrictions are not a ban on alcohol sales or on alcohol companies doing business in Ghana. Rather, they are advertising and sponsorship restrictions issued under Section 148 of the Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851), which prevent alcoholic beverages from being associated with sporting activities.

The FDA’s guidelines also prohibit alcohol advertisements from appealing to people under 18 and restrict links between alcohol and activities requiring care or skill, including sport. VAST Ghana maintains that these protections remain necessary precisely because football attracts large young audiences, both in stadiums and through broadcast and social-media coverage.

The potential Guinness Ghana deal represents a significant sum for the Ghana Premier League, and the GFA’s concern about lost revenue is understandable. Football administration often faces pressure to find sponsors, improve club finances, and make the domestic league more competitive and attractive to fans.

But VAST Ghana’s position raises a broader policy question: should alcohol brands be allowed to fund institutions that children follow closely? The organisation’s answer is no. It argues that the responsibility to protect children should not be traded for sponsorship income, however valuable that income may be to clubs and leagues.

The controversy has exposed a tension between sports development and public-health regulation in Ghana. Parliament’s Youth and Sports Committee chair, Dr Ernest Norgbey, has suggested that the Sports Fund Act permits beverage advertising at sporting events, while VAST Ghana disputes the claim that the Act overrides the FDA’s alcohol-advertising restrictions.

As the debate continues, the decision will likely shape more than football financing. It will test whether Ghana chooses to expand commercial sponsorship opportunities in sport or preserve strict limits on alcohol marketing around activities with a substantial young audience. For VAST Ghana, the choice is clear: children’s health and protection must come before commercial opportunity.

title: Seb Atkinson injury latest as Gloucester Rugby star limps off in England win
article_text:
England boss Steve Borthwick faces having to make yet another change to his midfield heading into Saturday’s Test against Japan, with Gloucester Rugby star Seb Atkinson a doubt for the Nations Championship game after taking a blow on Sunday.

Atkinson excelled in the 12 jersey for England in the 45-22 win over the Wallabies yesterday, as part of a slick-looking backline that saw his midfield partner Henry Slade named player of the match.

But Atkinson’s game against Australia was cut short in the 64th minute, with the 24-year-old limping off in clear discomfort in the second half of his eighth cap.

After having to bide his time, Atkinson has started in the 12 jersey for England's last six successive Test matches, plus the England A warm-up fixture out in France in June to establish himself in what has been a problem position for a number of years.

Speaking post-match, England head coach Steve Borthwick speculated that he does not expect Atkinson to be out for a significant period, with Tests against New Zealand and then the finals weekend of the new competition to come after facing Japan, which lost 28-21 to Wales at Principality Stadium on Saturday.

Borthwick said on Sunday: “Seb looks like a hip, hopefully nothing. We don’t think that’s anything long-term, but he’s very sore and bruised.

“We’re talking days to recover, maybe not available next weekend, but it’s really too early for me to say that.”

England are yet to add any players to their squad ahead of the Japan Test, with Exeter Chiefs winger Manny Feyi-Waboso also suffering an ankle injury which Borthwick said will require ‘more investigation.’

Should Atkinson miss the tie against Japan on Saturday, the other unused centres in the squad are Northampton’s Fraser Dingwell and Sale Sharks’ Joe Marchant and of course Gloucester’s Will Joseph, although the latter two are really more outside centre options.

Bath’s Max Ojomoh also impressed for England A on Friday night in their 59-24 win against Argentina XV at the Rec, with Cherry and Whites scrum-half Caolan Englefield named the player of the match.

title: Glasgow Warriors begin search for managing director with Kenny Brown to step down
article_text:
Kenny Brown will step down as Glasgow Warriors managing director at the end of next month.

Brown has been part of Glasgow Warriors since 2018 and took over as managing director in 2025 following the departure of Al Kellock.

The 45-year-old will depart to take up a new opportunity with his family in Australia, leaving with the club in a strong position both on and off the pitch.

“Leaving Glasgow Warriors has been a very difficult decision for me to make,” said Brown.

“Over the last seven years, I have loved my time at the club. Growing up in the west of Scotland, I have always had a real passion and attachment to Glasgow Warriors which will stay with me forever.

“I am incredibly proud of what we have achieved during my time here. Glasgow Warriors is in a strong position, with a talented squad and a group of people working tirelessly behind the scenes to help the club succeed.

“It has been a real team effort, and I have relied on the support of our players, coaches, staff, commercial partners and supporters throughout my time here. I want to thank everyone for their commitment and hard work, and for making Glasgow Warriors such a special club to be part of.

“While I am excited about what lies ahead for my family and me, I will leave with enormous pride in what we have accomplished together and will always look back on my time at Glasgow Warriors with great affection.”

Brown joined Glasgow Warriors in 2018, having previously held roles with Scottish Rugby, sportscotland and Premiership Rugby.

He became Team Manager in 2019 before progressing to Head of Operations in 2021.

He was appointed interim Managing Director in September 2025 following Al Kellock’s departure to become Scottish Rugby Head of Performance Pathways, before being confirmed in the role on a permanent basis in March 2026.

Glasgow Warriors head coach Franco Smith said: “Kenny has been a tremendous support to me and the coaching team, and I have really valued the relationship we have built over the last few years.

“He understands the demands of professional rugby and the importance of creating the right environment for our players and staff to perform. He has always been committed to helping the team and the wider club achieve its ambitions, and I am grateful for everything he has done to support us.

“Of course, we are disappointed to be losing Kenny, but this is an exciting opportunity for him and his family, and we wish them every happiness as they begin this next chapter. He leaves with our very best wishes and with the respect and affection of everyone at the club.”

David White, the interim CEO of Scottish Rugby, added: “Kenny has made a significant contribution to Glasgow Warriors over many years, and his appointment as managing director was a natural progression following his outstanding service to the club in a number of roles.

“While we will be sorry to see Kenny leave, we are fully supportive of his decision and want to see our people take opportunities that are right for them and their families. That is an important part of the culture we want to build across Scottish Rugby, and we wish Kenny and his family every happiness as they start this next chapter.”

The club will work closely with Brown over the coming weeks to ensure a smooth transition ahead of his departure at the end of December.

Further details on the recruitment of a new managing director "will be communicated in due course" the club added.

BKB coverage in the UK and Ireland is broadcast on the YouTube channel of major sports radio network TalkSport.

title: Coventry Building Society opens Sky Blue Line for fans
article_text:
Coventry City supporters can now speak straight to the dressing room. Coventry Building Society has launched The Sky Blue Line, a phone line where fans can record messages of support for the club’s players, with prizes for callers.

The campaign marks the building society’s partnership with the club and was created by Ear to the Ground. It opens with a hero film starring Coventry City head coach Frank Lampard and former manager Harry Redknapp, alongside Coventry City supporters drawn from the agency’s Fan Intelligence Network, a global community of fans whose insights shaped the idea.

The next phase turns the messages back on the squad. Players will be filmed listening and reacting to what supporters have recorded, giving fans a view of what their words mean to the team.

Ear to the Ground is also distributing the campaign directly through supporter groups. The aim is to raise awareness of Coventry Building Society’s role at the club and to strengthen its link with the Coventry City fanbase.

Jon Badger, Senior Sponsorship Manager at Coventry Building Society, said, “Our partnership with Coventry City FC is all about celebrating the fans and the community around the club. Owen Laverty, Chief Brand Officer at Ear to the Ground, said, “This is fan-powered creative in action. Turning real fan insights into an idea that brings Coventry Building Society’s partnership to life, with the passion of Coventry City supporters at its heart.”

Ear to the Ground was named Agency of the Year at the 2026 SIAs, its third win in the category. The agency previously took home the award in 2024 and 2021.

title: Ex-Sevens speedster called up as Argentina add four players to squad
article_text:
Argentina are awaiting the outcome of the Head Injury Assessment (HIA) protocol to see if captain Julián Montoya will be fit to lead them into battle against Italy in Genoa this Saturday.

Montoya, who has captained Los Pumas more than any other player, suffered a head injury in Friday night’s 42-12 defeat by Ireland in Dublin.

Pablo Matera will most likely take on the armband if Montoya is unavailable, having led the team in his absence in three Tests in August and September.

Hookers Bautista Bernasconi and Facundo Bosch have been called up as cover. Bernasconi has three caps and Bosch 11, but neither has a single Test start between them.

With utility back Juan Cruz Mallia facing a potentially lengthy spell on the sidelines due to the knee injury he picked up at the Aviva Stadium, Los Pumas have brought in uncapped Zebre player Tobias Wade, a former star of the sevens circuit.

Wade joined Zebre after impressing for Los Pampas in their 2026 Super Rugby Americas title-winning season.

As a sevens player before that, Wade won 10 tournament titles in a golden period for Los Pumas Sevens between 2022-25.

The quartet of new additions is completed by another potential debutant, Matias Medrano, who is a replacement for Rodrigo Martinez at prop.

Meanwhile, back-row forward Facundo Isa returns to Los Pumas’ training camp after being released to play for Pau in the Top 14 this weekend. The 33-year-old won the last of his 53 caps against England in July 2025.

Argentina have won their last nine matches against Italy dating back to 2008, and have achieved a record winning margin in each of the last three clashes, the most recent being 50-18 in Udine in 2024.

A repeat of that scoreline would be most welcome after failing to win any of their last five games, with the Ireland setback the worst of the lot.

title: Gael Monfils’ defended after controversial decision to become France’s Davis Cup captain
article_text:
Gael Monfils has a very big job on his hands after becoming France’s Davis Cup captain.

Monfils retired from tennis in 2026, but it has not taken long for the Frenchman to find his latest role in the sport.

He has replaced Paul-Henri Mathieu and he will be looking to win the Davis Cup for France for the first time in 2017, but they did not even qualify for the Finals this year.

There has been a slight backlash about Monfils’ appointment, due to his inexperience as a coach, but Gilles Simon has backed the decision.

Simon, who is currently the head of performance for the FFT (France Federation Tennis), said: “But honestly, when you think about it, if you want to bring a huge wave of freshness and shine a huge spotlight on the Davis Cup, I think it will bring a lot.

“It’s not as if he left the tour a long time ago. He knows absolutely every player, foreign and French alike. So if the question is whether he’ll be up to date with what’s going on, of course he will.

“The French team means a great deal to him. He has answered the call an enormous number of times. He was often there when we played the finals. He performed at a level in the Davis Cup that I never saw any other player of my generation reach.”

France do not have the biggest stars in the world currently, which has led to their relatively poor performances over the years since winning the tournament in 2017.

Monfils will be able to pick from the likes of Corentin Moutet, Quentin Halys, Ugo Humbert, Arthur Fils, and Luca Van Assche, but only one players, Fils, is currently ranked inside the top 10.

The rest of France’s players are ranked outside the top 30 of the rankings, so it will be difficult for them to compete against the likes of Spain, Italy, and Czech Republic at the very top of the tournament.

Nevertheless, Monfils has an impressive record for France at the Davis Cup that he will be looking to replicate as a coach.

He retired with a 12-3 win-loss record for France in singles action and he reached the final of the tournament during the 2014 season.

Monfils and France lost 3-1 to Switzerland in the final, but that one point was earned when the Frenchman stunned Roger Federer in a three-set contest, so he knows what it takes to perform at the very top of the Davis Cup.

title: WTGL launch day provides a glimpse into golf's strange new world
article_text:
The WTGL officially entered the world in Palm Beach Gardens, Fla., on Sunday afternoon with a 3-1 victory for Los Angeles Golf Club over New York Golf Club — which are words that only make sense if you’ve been paying attention to the regular ol’ TGL, the men’s version of the league, which features the same team names and logos and home stadium and proclivity for thumping bass.

But if you do know what the TGL is, and you know its tendencies and oddities, and you were wondering how the women’s version of simulator, primetime, made-for-TV golf looks up close, the answer is: It looks … pretty similar to the men’s version!

On the whole, that’s probably the biggest takeaway from match 1 of the WTGL: It was familiar. Familiar in the sense that it was judged on a different scale from tournament golf. Familiar in the feeling that the real scoreboard was counted in engagements and impressions and views and shares. Familiar in the sentiment that what mattered wasn’t who won, but whether they won interestingly.

The good news: It was interesting on Sunday. Even though the six women participating in Sunday’s match had little time to prepare for the oddities of simulator golf, they hardly looked out of place at the SoFi Center. Both teams enjoyed long birdie makes and near-aces and Belichickian hammer-throws and a Solheim Cup-worthy array of fist-pumps in match 1. They played without any real competitive hiccups, and they showed a willingness to lean into the goofiness.

Also deserving of kudos was the creation of the first-ever WTGL “red carpet.” The league encouraged each of the six players in the inaugural match to show up in their Sunday best, enjoying full hair-and-makeup treatment before they arrived to find a photo-and-interview area outside the arena similar to what you’d see at an awards show. The decision was clearly welcomed by the players, who raved about the experience afterward.

“I don’t have much of an opportunity to dress up like that, so it was a lot of fun. I’ve never done that coming to a golf tournament before,” said Michelle Wie West. “I hope players really lean into it because I think it can be another way that we can really show our story through fashion. I think that’s so fun.”

Wie West’s excitement was well founded: Athlete fashion is having a cultural moment in the 2020s, and athletes across the pro sports spectrum are using their attire as a means of showcasing their personality. (The NFL certainly knows this to be true; the league hired its first “fashion editor” in 2024 solely to help players show their personality on game days.) If the WTGL is in the business of generating attention, there are few more effective approaches than convincing its players to speak the language of broader culture.

The red carpet was a no-brainer for these ends. It generated attention. It was interesting. It cost almost nothing. And it made the players happy.

“I rarely these days get to have my makeup done, hair done and wear heels all at the same time,” said Alison Lee. “I think it’s been a couple years since that’s happened, so it was just nice to get my picture taken; I’m not going to lie.”

Of course, not every moment of Sunday was picture perfect. Both teams faced some of the — erhm, eccentricities — of simulator golf, when shots traveled in ways the masters of precision were evidently unfamiliar with. (E.g., Lydia Ko suggested a 9-iron with shoestring backspin was the first such 9-iron spin rate of her life as a golfer, per her live microphone.)

But perhaps the biggest concern had little to do with the competition at all: It was the fact that few sports fans likely even knew it was happening. The first match of the new league aired on ESPN — a win — smack-dab in the middle of a crowded NFL Sunday. While the development was understandable given the WTGL’s desire to air its big debut on a major national network, it worked against the league’s initial sell to the public, which was predicated on maximizing the TV interest of live golf.

Not every match has to be ideally placed for the WTGL to work on TV in the long run, but it certainly stands out that the new league faces such an immediate headwind in generating viewership. It also stands out that seven of the WTGL’s 15 scheduled matches for season 1 will compete with either an NFL Sunday or Monday Night Football.

It stands out because the NFL’s dominance comes back to its ability to do two things at once: land ratings and attention. If the goal is to give the LPGA stars a chance to showcase their personalities, routinely fighting against the largest monolith in televised sports could prove obstructive.

Of course, a league can justify success beyond TV ratings in many ways. The WTGL presents opportunities for player profile growth and genuine social media virality. It can also push the LPGA into the everyday golf conversation during a time of the year when little consequential golf is being played. And it’s fair to argue that airtime on ESPN and ABC is valuable for the LPGA regardless of competition, because such national TV audiences are so hard to come by.

These counterpoints provide cover to the WTGL if the TV ratings wind up flopping. But in many ways, these counterpoints alone serve as proof that the WTGL might be best served redefining its own barometer for success. If the world of cultural cachet and media relevance has grown beyond the influence of Nielsen ratings, then the upside for a league like the WTGL exists far outside the typical bounds of televised sports.

title: Look back at Emma Raducanu’s run to the 2026 HSBC Championships final
article_text:
Let’s take you back to June earlier this year. Clear skies, hot temperatures, and a Queen’s Club campaign to remember from Britain’s Emma Raducanu.

The then British No.1 was one of the stars of the 2026 HSBC Championships – reaching her first WTA 500 final in front of a home crowd at The Queen’s Club.

Now, Raducanu has announced that she is set to return to West London next summer, with tickets set to go on sale at 10:00 on Tuesday 10 November.

While the excitement gears up for another fortnight of world-class tennis at the HSBC Championships in June, take a look back at Raducanu’s impressive final run.

Raducanu made a fast and efficient start to the HSBC Championships against Anna Blinkova.

The British star showed no signs of pre-match nerves out on the Andy Murray Arena as she stormed to a 6-0, 6-3 victory in just one hour.

It was a statement performance for her first match of the season on grass. Raducanu won 70% of points against her opponent’s first serve, and her return game became a key factor throughout her path to the final.

Next up, seventh seed Sorana Cirstea, who was coming off the back of a semi-final run in Rome and a quarter-final at Roland Garros.

Playing one of the in-form stars on the WTA Tour, Raducanu recorded her first top-20 victory in over a year, coming through 6-4, 6-2.

Raducanu showcased her attacking style against Cirstea, winning 61% of the points with four shots or fewer, and propelled herself into the quarter-finals for the second year in a row.

Having lost just nine games in two matches, Raducanu was performing at a high level on the grass, and more was yet to come.

With a complete washout on Thursday and more delays on Friday, Raducanu didn’t get to play her quarter-final against Kamilla Rakhimova until Saturday.

Raducanu raced out to a set and 3-1 lead before slipping on court, which forced her to take a medical time-out. Rakhimova managed to edge 4-3 in front, but when things got tough, the British star rose to the challenge.

Despite missing the chance to serve for the match at 5-4, Raducanu got over the line at the second attempt, sealing a 6-3, 7-5 victory.

She joined Katie Boulter as one of two Brits in the semi-finals – only the second time that had happened at a WTA 500-level event.

A few hours after her quarter-final, Raducanu was back on court to face one of the rising stars of the WTA Tour – Iva Jovic.

Jovic had been in impressive form, knocking out 2025 HSBC Championships and Wimbledon runner-up Amanda Anisimova in the quarter-finals, and was looking to make her biggest grass-court final.

Despite playing a match earlier in the day, Raducanu put in arguably her best performance of the season against the sixth seed.

The former US Open champion kept her foot on the gas, attacking on a quarter of the points played against Jovic. She broke the American five times in a convincing 6-2, 6-2 victory to book her place in a first WTA 500 final without dropping a set.

Awaiting her in the final was Croatian Donna Vekic.

Vekic came into the tournament as a lucky loser but got better and better as the event went on – defeating Boulter in the semi-final.

The world No.76 put together one of the most dominant sets in Queen’s Club final history – taking it 6-0 in 28 minutes.

However, Raducanu had her chances in the second set. She quickly turned momentum on its head, took a 5-2 lead, and had two set points a few games later.

Vekic refused to let go of the set and eventually went on to win the last five games in a row to seal her second career grass-court title with a 6-0, 7-5 victory.

It was a tough result for the British star, who later revealed that she had been dealing with an injury that put her out for the rest of the season.

In 2027, Raducanu will return to The Queen’s Club with ambitions of going one further and lifting a first title on home soil.

Watch Raducanu and more of the world’s best tennis stars at the HSBC Championships – tickets on sale now.

title: Lakshya Sen targets World Tour Finals qualification at Kumamoto Masters
article_text:
Fresh from his Hylo Open title, the Indian eighth seed faces Chi Yu Jen in Japan, with the Hong Kong Open also crucial to his qualification hopes.

Bolstered by a timely title triumph in Germany, ace Indian shuttler Lakshya Sen will look to strengthen his bid for a place in the season-ending BWF World Tour Finals when he competes at the USD 500,000 Kumamoto Masters Japan Super 500 tournament, beginning here on Tuesday.

World No. 13 Lakshya, who ended a difficult phase by returning to the podium at the Hylo Open, will open his campaign against world No. 24 Chi Yu Jen of Chinese Taipei.

The eighth-seeded Indian is currently 10th in the BWF World Tour rankings and needs to break into the top eight to qualify for the season-ending tournament in China.

The 25-year-old from Almora has a 1-1 head-to-head record against Chi, and a strong showing this week and at next week's Hong Kong Open Super 500 could be enough to secure his place.

The BWF World Tour Finals will be held from December 9 to 13.

India's Kidambi Srikanth, who reached the US Open final in June this year, is also in the men's singles draw here. He will face Denmark's Rasmus Gemke.

In women's singles, Malvika Bansod will take on fifth seed Tomoka Miyazaki of Japan.

World No. 6 and sixth seeds Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will look to rediscover their winning touch after three successive first-round exits since winning the China Masters title.

The Indian pair, which failed to defend its gold medal at the Asian Games, will face fifth seeds Wang Chang and Xie Haonan of China.

Satwik and Chirag, who also won the Singapore Open earlier this year, are 12th in the BWF World Tour rankings with 58,550 points.

However, BWF rules allow a maximum of two pairs from a country to qualify for the World Tour Finals, provided they finish inside the top eight.

Currently, only Indonesia and Malaysia have two pairs each inside the top eight, with South Korea, England, China and Denmark also represented.

Third seeds Hariharan Amsakarunan and M.R. Arjun will face Malaysia's Aaron Chia and Soh Wooi Yik.

In women's doubles, Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand will take on Japan's Hinata Suzuki and Nao Yamakita.

The mixed doubles pairing of Hariharan and Tanisha Crasto will face top seeds Jiang Zhen Bang and Wei Ya Xin of China, while Dhruv Rawat and K. Maneesha will face fourth seeds Ye Hong Wei and Nicole Gonzales Chan of Chinese Taipei.

title: Japan Masters 2026 Starts Today, 11 Indonesian Representatives Ready to Compete, Check the Schedule and Opponents
article_text:
KUMAMOTO, Aktualita.co - The Kumamoto Japan Masters 2026 badminton tournament officially enters its first day on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. A total of 11 Indonesian representatives are preparing to face the competition in the BWF World Tour Super 500 event, which will take place at the Kumamoto Prefectural Gymnasium, Japan, until Sunday, November 15, 2026.

The Japan Masters 2026 is one of the important tournaments leading up to the end of this season's BWF World Tour. In addition to competing for a total prize pool of 500,000 US dollars, the players also have the opportunity to collect world ranking points.

Indonesia is relying on a number of seeded players, including Fajar Alfian/Muhammad Shohibul Fikri in the men's doubles sector, Putri Kusuma Wardani in women's singles, as well as Alwi Farhan and Moh. Zaki Ubaidillah in men's singles.

However, the preparation of the Merah Putih squad underwent changes after the All Indonesia Badminton Association (PBSI) withdrew two pairs from the participant list.

With these changes, Indonesia now has 11 representatives spread across five competition sectors.

The Japan Masters 2026 will last for six days, with matches starting from the qualifying round and the first round on Tuesday (10/11/2026).

Based on the organizer's schedule, the first day's matches are scheduled to start at 09:00 Japan time or 08:00 WITA.

- Tuesday, November 10, 2026: Qualifying and round of 32.

- Wednesday, November 11, 2026: Continuation of the round of 32.

- Thursday, November 12, 2026: Round of 16.

- Friday, November 13, 2026: Quarter-finals.

- Saturday, November 14, 2026: Semi-finals.

- Sunday, November 15, 2026: Finals for all sectors.

The quarter-final and semi-final matches are scheduled to start at 09:00 WITA, while the final matches on Sunday will start at 10:00 WITA.

The schedule for each player may change according to the order of matches, court conditions, and the duration of previous matches.

Indonesia is fielding a mix of young players and experienced athletes in this tournament.

In the men's singles sector, attention is focused on Alwi Farhan, who is scheduled to face Chinese Taipei representative Lin Chun-Yi in the opening match.

The duel is expected to be tight because both players have attacking abilities and rely on a fast-paced game.

Meanwhile, Moh. Zaki Ubaidillah, familiarly known as Ubed, will face Brian Yang from Canada. Meanwhile, Muhamad Yusuf must pass the qualifying round first by facing Yoo Tae-bin from South Korea.

In the women's singles sector, Indonesia only has one representative, namely Putri Kusuma Wardani. She is scheduled to meet the host player, Riko Gunji, in the first round.

The men's doubles sector is one of Indonesia's mainstays through Fajar Alfian/Muhammad Shohibul Fikri, who are the second seeds.

Fajar/Fikri will face Hiroki Okamura/Kyohei Yamashita from Japan. Meanwhile, Sabar Karyaman Gutama/Moh Reza Pahlevi Isfahani will meet the Chinese pair, Hu Ke Yuan/Liang Wei Keng.

In the women's doubles sector, Indonesia is relying on Febriana Dwipuji Kusuma/Meilysa Trias Puspitasari and Amallia Cahaya Pratiwi/Siti Fadia Silva Ramadhanti.

Febriana/Meilysa are scheduled to meet Chang Ching Hui/Yang Ching Tun from Chinese Taipei. Meanwhile, Tiwi/Fadia will face Rui Hirokami/Sayaka Hobara from Japan.

Meanwhile, three Indonesian pairs are appearing in the mixed doubles sector.

Amri Syahnawi/Nita Violina Marwah will face Ruben Garcia/Lucia Rodriguez from Spain. Marwan Faza/Aisyah Salsabila Putri Pranata will meet Yuta Watanabe/Maya Taguchi from Japan.

Another pair, Dejan Ferdinansyah/Felisha Alberta Nathaniel Pasaribu, is scheduled to face Gao Jia Xuan/Wu Meng Ying from China.

Ahead of the start of the Japan Masters 2026, PBSI decided to cancel the participation of two pairs, namely Devin Artha Wahyudi/Ali Faathir Rayhan and Rachel Allessya Rose/Febi Setianingrum.

The decision was taken after the coaching team evaluated the performance and readiness of the athletes following the series of tournaments in Europe.

Head Coach of Indonesian Men's Doubles, Antonius Budi Ariantho, explained that Devin/Faathir need additional time to improve their performance before returning to international competition.

"We withdrew Devin/Faathir's participation from the Kumamoto Masters 2026 because the evaluation from the three previous tournaments in Europe showed results that were not good enough," said Antonius, Monday (9/11/2026).

The pair is subsequently directed to undergo training in preparation for the Hong Kong Open and the Syed Modi India International 2026.

Meanwhile, Rachel/Febi are considered not yet in an ideal condition to return to competition.

Head Coach of PBSI Women's Doubles, Karel Mainaky, chose to provide time for improvement at the Cipayung National Training Center so that the pair can prepare themselves for the next competition season.

The withdrawal of the two pairs reduced the number of Indonesian representatives from the initial plan of 13 to 11 participants.

The attention of Indonesian badminton fans is also focused on Fajar Alfian/Muhammad Shohibul Fikri.

Their status as the second seeds makes the pair one of the candidates to be reckoned with in the fight for the men's doubles title.

However, the competition will not be easy because a number of strong pairs from China, South Korea, and Japan are also enlivening the tournament.

In women's singles, Putri Kusuma Wardani faces her own challenges as the only Indonesian representative.

Meanwhile, Alwi Farhan and Moh. Zaki Ubaidillah have the opportunity to show the development of their game when facing opponents with international experience.

The Japan Masters also holds important records for Indonesia.

Gregoria Mariska Tunjung won the women's singles sector in the inaugural edition in 2023. A year later, Fajar Alfian/Muhammad Rian Ardianto won the men's doubles title in the 2024 edition.

title: Seven nets record viewership for RLWC semi-final coverage
article_text:
The men’s and women’s semi-finals of the 2026 Rugby League World Cup delivered record-breaking viewership for domestic rights holder Seven Network as millions of Australians tuned in to watch the blockbuster tie-ups.

The tournament, being held across Australia, New Zealand, and Papua New Guinea, has reached its final stages with Australia’s Kangaroos (men’s) and Jillaroos (women’s) national teams advancing to the finals against New Zealand in a big win for domestic broadcasters.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The highest figure of the weekend came with Seven’s coverage of the men’s semi-final between Australia and Samoa yesterday (November 8), which averaged 2.05 million viewers, peaking at 3.68 million, making the game the most-watched RLWC match ever.

The match also had an audience of 733,000 on the 7plus Sport streaming service, making it also the largest streaming audience for an RLWC game and for an international rugby league game.

The men’s other semi-final between New Zealand and Tonga on Saturday evening (November 7) reached 2.84 million, with an average audience of 1.47 million, including 531,000 on 7plus Sport.

Meanwhile, Sunday evening’s women’s semi-final between Australia and Fiji became the most-watched women’s RLWC game ever, reaching 1.81 million, with an average audience of 903,000. The match also drew 241,000 viewers on 7plus Sport.

Seven Network head of RLWC Lesley Tapsall said: “It’s been an incredible weekend for rugby league, with audiences right across the country turning to Seven in record numbers for two exhilarating semi-finals between Australia and Samoa and the Jillaroos and Fiji.

“These numbers reflect the incredible appetite for international rugby league and the growing interest in both the men’s and women’s games.

“We’re incredibly proud to deliver these moments to Australians live and free, and there’s still so much more to come on Seven this week.”

Seven Network secured the exclusive Australian rights to the RLWC, which it has been airing live and free on its linear Seven channel and 7plus streaming service since October 15.

The men’s and women’s RLWC finals are scheduled for Sunday, November 15.

The 2026 tri-tournament RLWC in Australia is a replacement for the 2025 RLWC, which was canceled after France withdrew from hosting the event for financial reasons.

Australia was then announced as the replacement host for the event to be staged a year later, with a reduced field of 10 men’s teams (from a previous 16), as well as eight-team women’s and wheelchair World Cups.

The majority of the games have been played in Australia, with four matches staged in Papua New Guinea, and two in New Zealand.

France was awarded the tournament in January 2022, which was delayed to October and November 2025, after the original co-hosts, the US and Canada, withdrew in 2018, ending the IRL’s plans to take the tournament out of Europe and Oceania for the first time.

The last Rugby League World Cup, hosted by England, was postponed to 2022 after Australia and New Zealand withdrew from playing it in 2021 due to the ongoing pandemic.

The latest shift of the tournament from 2025 to 2026 comes as part of a revised calendar that will see the following men's edition held in 2030 and the women's and wheelchair World Cups staged separately.

title: Denmark claims four titles at Norwegian International
article_text:
Denmark enjoyed a successful week at the FZ FORZA Norwegian International 2026, claiming four of the five titles at the Future Series tournament in Sandefjord.

The only title to escape Danish hands came in mixed doubles, where Finland's Ananda Galvani Daniswara and Estonia's Elisaveta Berik defeated Denmark's Tobias Rønbøg/Maria Søgård Andersen in three games, 19-21 21-17 21-11.

Denmark bounced back with four victories in the remaining finals. Mathias Solgaard defeated compatriot Alexander Ringbæk 21-12 21-15 in an all-Danish men's singles final, while Laura Fløj Thomsen secured the women's singles title with a straight-games victory over Indonesia's Irdina Naurah Mirza.

In women's doubles, Maria Søgård Andersen/Rebecca Thorup defeated fellow Danes Emma Jonassen/Marie Viscovich 21-15 21-16.

Mikkel Eilersen Bouet/Oliver Geisler completed the Danish success, beating Finland's Juha Honkanen/Jesper Paul 21-12 21-14 in the men's doubles final.

With four titles and several all-Danish finals, it was a strong showing from the Danish team in Sandefjord.
